relative.description: Largest difference as a share of the other system's amount still counted as agreeing, e.g. 0.0001; the larger of the two tolerances applies (default 0).

irr.description: Largest IRR difference still counted as agreeing, as a decimal (default 0.0001, one basis point).

tools.name: calc_reconcile_cam
tools.title: Tie out CAM reconciliations against another system's results
tools.description: Reconcile FactLot's CAM reconciliation for one expense pool with another system's per-tenant results (Yardi or any other; parity is not claimed and is untested against a real export): give the calc_cam_reconciliation_batch input plus, per tenant, what the other system reported (share, gross-up, cap limit and reduction, admin fee, base-year or stop deduction, billed amount, estimates, balance; billed_amount required) and a tolerance. Returns per tenant and line FactLot's amount, the other amount, the difference and whether it is within tolerance, tenants missing on either side, and likely causes worded as hypotheses to check: a different pro rata share (and, when every share differs by one factor, the pool's denominator), or a FactLot rerun that matches the other system with lines left to the default controllable: true set uncontrollable, the cap's base year one year off, the other cap method, the other gross-up target or no gross-up, the admin fee before or after and within or outside the cap, or no fee on uncontrollable lines; and differing estimates paid. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.reconcile_cam@1, every step, and any warnings.

year.description: Calendar or lease year being reconciled.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable. Default true; under a cap, lines left unset are named in warnings.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee). Default false; with a gross-up, lines left unset are named in warnings.

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: The building's operating expense pool for the year, entered once for every tenant: category, amount, controllable, recoverable, variable, admin_fee_applies.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0).

name.description: Tenant or suite label, unique, e.g. "Suite 200 – Acme".

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up).

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

excluded_categories.description: Expense categories this tenant's lease excludes, treated as recoverable: false for this tenant only. Each must match a category in expenses.

admin_fee_excluded_categories.description: Expense categories this tenant's lease keeps out of the admin fee base, treated as admin_fee_applies: false for this tenant only. Each must match a category in expenses.

tenants.description: Every tenant to reconcile (up to 500): each one's share, structure (base year or stop), cap, admin fee, occupancy, estimates paid, and lease-specific exclusions. Each statement equals calc_cam_reconciliation for that tenant.

cam.description: The FactLot CAM input for one expense pool, exactly as calc_cam_reconciliation_batch takes it (the same pool, shares and lease terms you entered in the other system).

system.description: Name of the system or file the results come from, echoed in the result, e.g. "Yardi CAM recon export" (free text).

pool.description: The pool these results are for, e.g. "CAM", echoed in the result.

tenant.description: Tenant as the other system names it; matched to cam.tenants[].name exactly, else ignoring case and punctuation.

pool.description: The other system's expense pool for this row, e.g. "CAM" (echoed; reconcile one pool per call).

pro_rata_share.description: The other system's pro rata share for the tenant, 0 < share ≤ 1.

gross_up_applied.description: Whether the other system grossed up variable expenses for this tenant.

grossed_up_expenses.description: The other system's pool after gross-up (the building amount before the tenant's share), USD.

cap_applied.description: Whether a cap reduced the other system's charge.

cap_limit.description: The other system's cap limit on the tenant's controllable share, USD.

cap_reduction.description: Amount the cap removed in the other system, USD.

admin_fee_applied.description: Whether the other system charged an admin fee.

admin_fee.description: The other system's admin or management fee for the tenant, USD.

structure_deduction.description: The other system's base-year or expense-stop deduction, USD.

billed_amount.description: What the other system billed the tenant for the year before estimates (FactLot's tenant_charge), USD.

estimates_paid.description: Estimates (prior billings) the other system credits for the year, USD.

balance_due.description: The other system's balance due (negative for a credit), USD.

tenants.description: The other system's per-tenant results for this pool. Give whatever it reports; billed_amount is required.

other.description: What the other system reported for the same pool and year.

tolerance.description: When two amounts agree: |FactLot − other| ≤ max(absolute, relative × |other|); shares within share. Default: 1.00 USD, 0, and 0.000001.

absolute.description: Largest difference, USD, still counted as agreeing (default 1.00).

relative.description: Largest difference as a share of the other system's amount still counted as agreeing, e.g. 0.0001; the larger of the two tolerances applies (default 0).

share.description: Largest pro rata share difference still counted as agreeing (default 0.000001).

tools.name: calc_tx_unequal_appraisal
tools.title: Texas unequal appraisal: median of adjusted comparables
tools.description: Evidence calculation only: not an appraisal or an opinion of value, not legal or tax advice, and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. The arithmetic of Tex. Tax Code §41.43(b)(3) and §42.26(a)(3), the subject's value against the median appraised value of a reasonable number of comparable properties appropriately adjusted. Takes 3–200 comparables chosen by the caller, each with its roll value and the caller's adjustments (percent, USD amount, or $/SF, each with a reason); optionally normalizes each comparable to value per SF of improvement or land area times the subject's area; applies percentages summed or compounded, then amounts; and returns every comparable's normalized and adjusted value, the sorted list, the median (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values), and the subject's value minus the median in USD (subject_minus_median) and as a fraction of the median (subject_minus_median_pct: 0.1554 means 15.54%, a decimal like every rate in FactLot, not 0.1554%), with the statutes cited. Warns on mixed value bases, §42.26(d) and the §23.231 limitation, comparables in another county, fewer than 5 comparables, total adjustments over 25%, a comparable identical to the subject, no adjustments at all (the median is then unadjusted), and, with normalize_by none, a comparable whose area differs from the subject's by more than 25%. Each comparable row carries flags (code and sentence, facts about the inputs, never a reason the tool drops anything): value per SF more than twice or less than half the subject's, a land-to-improvement area ratio more than twice or less than half the subject's, an area the subject has but the comparable lacks. Optional label (up to 80 characters) and address (up to 120) on the subject and each comparable are echoed in the result (subject_label, subject_address, comparables[i].label and .address) for reports. registry_tx_equity_candidates returns calc_args, its candidates in this tool's input shape, for the caller to review and edit before calling this tool. It does not choose comparables, invent adjustments, or say whether to protest. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.tx_unequal_appraisal@1, every step, and any warnings.

tax_year.description: Tax year of the values compared, e.g. 2027. Decides which text of §42.26(d) applies.

id.description: Identifier of the subject property, e.g. its FactLot parcel ID.

label.description: A name to print for this property in reports (up to 80 characters), e.g. its street address or the caller's comp number. Echoed in the result; not used in the arithmetic.

address.description: The property's address as the caller wants it printed (up to 120 characters). Echoed in the result; not used in the arithmetic.

county_fips.description: Texas county FIPS code, 3 digits, e.g. "201" for Harris. Optional; used only to warn when a comparable is in a different county (appraisal district) from the subject.

value.description: The subject's value from the appraisal roll (or the value at issue), USD.

value_basis.description: Which roll value this is: "appraised" (after any limitation) or "market". Use the same basis for the subject and every comparable.

improvement_area_sf.description: Improvement (building) area, SF. Required when normalize_by is improvement_area_sf.

land_area_sf.description: Land area, SF. Required when normalize_by is land_area_sf.

circuit_breaker_23_231.description: Whether the subject is subject to the §23.231 limitation on appraised value (the circuit breaker for non-homestead property). Only used for warnings about which value §42.26(d) compares.

subject.description: The property whose value is compared.

normalize_by.description: "none" compares whole values. "improvement_area_sf" or "land_area_sf" converts each comparable to value per SF of that area and multiplies by the subject's same area before adjusting; the subject and every comparable must then have that area.

adjustment_combine.description: "sum" adds a comparable's percentage adjustments and applies the total once (the usual adjustment grid); "compound" multiplies (1 + each percentage).

id.description: Identifier of the comparable, e.g. its FactLot parcel ID or account number. Must differ from the subject's and from every other comparable's.

label.description: A name to print for this property in reports (up to 80 characters), e.g. its street address or the caller's comp number. Echoed in the result; not used in the arithmetic.

address.description: The property's address as the caller wants it printed (up to 120 characters). Echoed in the result; not used in the arithmetic.

county_fips.description: Texas county FIPS code, 3 digits, e.g. "201" for Harris. Optional; used only to warn when a comparable is in a different county (appraisal district) from the subject.

value.description: The comparable's value from the appraisal roll, USD.

value_basis.description: Which roll value this is: "appraised" (after any limitation) or "market". Use the same basis for the subject and every comparable.

improvement_area_sf.description: Improvement (building) area, SF. Required when normalize_by is improvement_area_sf.

land_area_sf.description: Land area, SF. Required when normalize_by is land_area_sf.

fact_id.description: FactLot fact ID of the comparable's value, if it came from the registry.

document_id.description: FactLot document ID of the source (e.g. the appraisal roll file).

locator.description: Where in the source the value is: row, account number, page.

as_of.description: Date the value was read or certified, YYYY-MM-DD.

citation.description: Where the comparable's value comes from. Passed through to the output unchanged.

adjustments.description: Adjustments to this comparable, each with a reason. Percentages are applied first (summed or compounded per adjustment_combine), then amounts and $/SF adjustments.

label.description: What the adjustment is for, e.g. "age", "size", "condition".

kind.description: "percent": a decimal share of the normalized value (0.05 for +5%, -0.02 for -2%); "amount": USD added to the value (negative to deduct); "psf": USD per SF of the normalizing area, multiplied by the subject's area (only with normalize_by other than "none").

value.description: The adjustment: a decimal between -1 and 1 for percent (0.05, not 5), else USD or USD/SF. Positive raises the comparable's value.

reason.description: Why the adjustment is made, in the caller's words (e.g. "comp built 1998, subject 2006"). Required: FactLot never invents an adjustment.

comparables.description: The comparable properties, 3 to 200, chosen by the caller. Values must be on the same basis as the subject's.

tools.name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline
tools.title: Texas property tax protest deadline
tools.description: Deadline to file a Texas property tax protest with the appraisal review board: the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice of appraised value was delivered, rolled past weekends and Texas legal holidays, plus a conservative file-by date (the last business day on or before the unadjusted deadline). status says where as_of (default: today in US Central time; echoed in as_of) falls: not_yet_open before January 1 of the tax year, open from then through the deadline, passed after it; days_remaining counts the days to the deadline (null once passed), and once passed next_season gives the same rule for the next tax year (May 15 basis). notes says what the rule does not cover (late protests, other §41.44 deadlines, §25.25 corrections) and which sections to read. Returns the statute citations, the rule's verification status and a disclaimer. Information about a statutory deadline: not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Verification status: verified. Cite rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@2 and its statutes.

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis).

as_of.description: Date the status is measured from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current date in US Central time (America/Chicago), when the call is answered; pass it to fix the date (for a report, or for El Paso and Hudspeth counties, which keep Mountain time).

tools.name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline_batch
tools.title: Texas property tax protest deadlines (batch)
tools.description: Texas property tax protest deadlines for many notices in one call (1–200 items, e.g. a consultant's client list): each item's id, tax year and, if known, notice delivery date. Each result is exactly what rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline returns for that item under rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@2 (deadline, unadjusted deadline, governing basis, conservative file-by date, skipped days, status, days_remaining, next_season, the item's warnings), echoed with its id; an item with invalid input carries its error and the others are still answered. One as_of (default: today in US Central time) applies to every item. summary counts the items per deadline, earliest first, with the earliest and latest deadline, and per status (by_status). The as_of used, the notes, the statute citations, the rule's verification status and the disclaimer appear once (value.as_of, value.notes, value.rule, value.disclaimer). A rules tool: never a registry lookup. Information about statutory deadlines: not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney; it does not say whether to protest. Verification status: verified. Cite rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline_batch@1 and its statutes.

id.description: Your label for this notice (a client, account or parcel number), echoed back with its result. Unique within the batch.

tax_year.description: Tax year being protested, e.g. 2026 (2000–2100). An invalid value is an error for this item only.

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis). An invalid date is an error for this item only.

items.description: The notices to compute deadlines for (1–200): each one's id, tax year and, if known, notice delivery date. Each result equals rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline for that item.

as_of.description: Date the status is measured from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current date in US Central time (America/Chicago), when the call is answered; pass it to fix the date (for a report, or for El Paso and Hudspeth counties, which keep Mountain time). One date for every item.

tools.name: id_parcel
tools.title: FactLot parcel ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a parcel from state FIPS, county FIPS, and the assessor's parcel number (APN). The same parcel always yields the same ID, offline. Use it as the join key across systems. APNs that differ only in where a separator falls ("12-34", "1-234") get different IDs; in a county with a documented fixed-width format the variants of one APN converge (NYC BBL "3-1234-56" = "3012340056").

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS code, e.g. "06" for California.

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS code, e.g. "037" for Los Angeles County.

apn.description: Assessor's parcel number exactly as the county prints it. Letter case and the separator characters are normalized; where a separator falls is kept, except in counties with a documented fixed-width format (NYC BBL, Los Angeles AIN, Cook County PIN, DC SSL).

tools.name: id_entity
tools.title: FactLot legal-entity ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a legal entity (LLC, LP, corporation, trust) from its registry jurisdiction and file number, or from its LEI (an LEI whose ISO 17442 check digits do not match is rejected).

jurisdiction.description: Registry jurisdiction, e.g. "us-de" for Delaware, or "lei" for a Legal Entity Identifier.

registry_number.description: File number issued by that registry, or the 20-character LEI (its ISO 17442 check digits are verified).

tools.name: id_space
tools.title: FactLot space (suite) ID
tools.description: FactLot ID for a suite or unit within a building, given the building's FactLot URN (from id_building). Suite designators are normalized: "Suite 100", "Ste 100" and "#100" agree, while "1-20" and "120" stay distinct.

building_urn.description: FactLot building URN from id_building, e.g. fl:building:us-11001:20002:208-massachusetts-ave-ne (a minted fl:building:<26-character token> also works).

suite.description: Suite or unit as written ("Suite 400", "STE 400", "#400", "3rd Floor" all normalize).

tools.name: id_building
tools.title: FactLot building ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a building from its street address: county FIPS, ZIP code, and street line. Every condominium unit, suite, and floor at the address gets the same building ID, offline. Pass it to id_space for a suite, or to registry_get to see the building's parcels.

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS code, e.g. "11" for the District of Columbia.

zip.description: 5-digit ZIP code of the address, e.g. "20002" (ZIP+4 accepted).

street.description: Street line: house number and street, e.g. "208 Massachusetts Ave NE". A suite, unit or floor is ignored, and so is anything after a comma (city, state).

tools.name: id_document
tools.title: FactLot document ID
tools.description: Content-addressed FactLot ID (SHA-256) for a document such as a lease, amendment, or estoppel.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the exact file bytes (preferred: every party gets the same ID).

text.description: Document text, UTF-8 encoded before hashing. Use only when bytes are unavailable.

tools.name: id_parse
tools.title: Parse a FactLot ID
tools.description: Validate a FactLot URN and return its kind, components, and short ID.

urn.description: A FactLot URN to validate, e.g. fl:parcel:us-06037:5432001012.

tools.name: fact_validate
tools.title: Validate a FactLot fact
tools.description: Check one FactLot fact against the published fact schema (spec/schemas/fact.json): subject URN, dotted predicate, as_of date, provenance, optional rights; unknown fields are rejected at every level. Rules: every fact except a computed one cites at least one source (an inferred fact cites the evidence it was inferred from); a computed fact names its formula or cites a source; valid_from is not after valid_to; a source span does not end before it starts. For Ingest predicates (lease.expiration_date, lease.rentable_area_sf, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) the value must have the predicate's shape and every source quote must state the value, by the same written-form rules as doc_verify_facts (a quote saying "2,500 square feet" does not support 1000). Not checked: that the quote is in the document, that the document or sha256 exists, that supersedes IDs exist, and quotes for other predicates; doc_verify_facts with the document's pages checks the quote. Returns { valid, issues }. Call before storing or sharing facts.

fact.description: A FactLot fact: subject, predicate, value, as_of, provenance (with sources), optional rights.

tools.name: doc_verify_facts
tools.title: Verify extracted document facts
tools.description: Check values YOU extracted from a document against its text, deterministically; FactLot runs no model. Send the pages as text and one candidate per value: {predicate, value, quote, page}. Each candidate is checked in order: (1) the value's shape (Ingest predicates such as lease.expiration_date YYYY-MM-DD, lease.pro_rata_share in (0, 1], ordered lease.base_rent_schedule steps; any other dotted predicate needs a non-empty value); (2) the quote, at least 12 characters, is on the cited page, where only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ (a word hyphenated across a line must keep its hyphen; a quote found on exactly one other page is accepted with the page corrected); (3) every number, date and party name in the value is written in the quote, in any common form: 1250000 matches "$1,250,000.00", 0.03 matches "3%" or "three percent", 2031-06-30 matches "June 30, 2031" or "6/30/2031"; text the lease states as written (a prohibited use, a carve-out, a protected use) is written in it as words, ignoring case, punctuation and line breaks; (4) a confidence you give below 0.8 holds it for review; (5) every other part of the value must be confirmed by the quote too: a true/false value, an enum or a summary not written in the quote holds the candidate for review, named in the reason. Verified means every part of the value was found in the quote. Returns verified (FactLot facts: method extracted, citing document_id, page, quote and character span, plus which value parts were checked and as what), needs_review (the quote is on the page but does not state the value: check consistency; low confidence: confidence; a part FactLot cannot confirm from the quote, such as a boolean: coverage) and rejected (wrong shape; quote missing, too short, or on several pages), each with a reason to act on. Not checked: meaning (a quote stating the number in another context passes), and whether the pages came from the file whose sha256 you give.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

document.description: The document the candidates were read from.

predicate.description: Dotted lower_snake predicate. Use an Ingest predicate (lease.expiration_date, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) for its value-shape and quote rules; any other predicate gets the generic rules.

value.description: The value you read, in the predicate's shape: dates YYYY-MM-DD, money and areas as plain numbers (1250000, not "$1.25M"), shares and rates as decimals (0.03 for 3%).

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page that states the value, at least 12 characters. Copy it exactly; only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ.

section.description: Section or clause as written, e.g. "§4.2(b)".

confidence.description: Your confidence 0–1. Below 0.8 the candidate goes to needs_review even if it verifies.

commencement.description: Only for lease.base_rent_schedule written by lease year (steps {lease_years: [1, 5], annual_rent_psf}): the commencement date the step dates are derived from, with its own quote. FactLot checks it like a lease.commencement_date candidate and derives each step: Lease Year N runs from the (N−1)th anniversary of the commencement date to the day before the next. If it does not verify, the schedule stays in needs_review.

quote.description: Verbatim text that states the commencement date, at least 12 characters.

page.description: 1-based page of this document the quote is on (it may differ from the rent table's page).

confirmation.description: A person's confirmation of the parts of the value no quote can prove (a true/false value, an enum such as a CAM cap method or kick-out party, a paraphrased summary). With it, a candidate whose only gaps are such parts is verified with method human_verified: the parts the quote confirmed are listed under checked and the rest under confirmed_by_person. It never overrides a quote that is not on the page, a number or date the quote does not state, or a confidence below 0.8.

by.description: The name or role of the PERSON who read the clause and confirmed the value, e.g. "J. Smith, lease administrator". FactLot does not authenticate it. Never set this for a value no person has read: an agent must not confirm its own extraction.

at.description: When the person confirmed it: YYYY-MM-DD, or an ISO 8601 timestamp with offset. A date is recorded on the fact as that day at 00:00 UTC.

note.description: What the person checked; returned with the result (the fact schema has no field for it).

candidates.description: Values you extracted, each with its quote and page.

as_of.description: Date the facts are stated as of (YYYY-MM-DD), usually today.

subject.description: FactLot URN the facts are about, e.g. your lease's fl:lease:… ID. Default: the document ID.

tools.name: doc_abstract_lease
tools.title: Lease abstract with amendments
tools.description: Current-state lease abstract from a lease and its amendments, with amendment precedence, as of as_of. Give each document's pages with the candidates you extracted (checked exactly as doc_verify_facts checks them), or the facts doc_verify_facts already returned for it (without pages only the value against its quote is rechecked, marked quote_on_page: false). Documents may come in any order: give the lease role original and each amendment role amendment with its effective_date (without a role the lease is inferred only when that is unambiguous, otherwise it is an input error; two or more amendments need effective dates). The original applies first, then amendments by effective_date; a later document's value for a predicate controls, and the earlier one moves to history and is linked through supersedes. An amendment effective after as_of is pending: its values are listed under pending and pending_facts with a warning and do not control. A rent schedule restated from a later date keeps the earlier steps before it (carried_forward). Each field gives its value, the controlling document, page, quote and fact, the superseded history, conflicts (two different values from one document, or from two documents of the same rank), pending values and open_items (a candidate for that predicate in the controlling or a later document that needs review or was rejected, so the value may not be final). FactLot only orders what you extracted: it does not find terms you missed, and an amendment that changes a term without restating it ("extended by 24 months") needs the resulting value extracted with that sentence as its quote, which the quote check will hold for review if the date is not written there.

role.description: Give it. Without one, a document is the original only when no document is marked original and it is the only one without a role (or without a role and an effective_date); otherwise it is an amendment, and input that leaves the original unclear is an error. Input order is never used.

effective_date.description: Amendment effective date (YYYY-MM-DD), required when there are two or more amendments: they apply in date order, and amendments effective the same day do not supersede each other (a different value is a conflict). An amendment effective after as_of is pending: its values are listed under pending and do not control the current abstract. Becomes valid_from on its facts.

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

predicate.description: Dotted lower_snake predicate. Use an Ingest predicate (lease.expiration_date, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) for its value-shape and quote rules; any other predicate gets the generic rules.

value.description: The value you read, in the predicate's shape: dates YYYY-MM-DD, money and areas as plain numbers (1250000, not "$1.25M"), shares and rates as decimals (0.03 for 3%).

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page that states the value, at least 12 characters. Copy it exactly; only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ.

section.description: Section or clause as written, e.g. "§4.2(b)".

confidence.description: Your confidence 0–1. Below 0.8 the candidate goes to needs_review even if it verifies.

commencement.description: Only for lease.base_rent_schedule written by lease year (steps {lease_years: [1, 5], annual_rent_psf}): the commencement date the step dates are derived from, with its own quote. FactLot checks it like a lease.commencement_date candidate and derives each step: Lease Year N runs from the (N−1)th anniversary of the commencement date to the day before the next. If it does not verify, the schedule stays in needs_review.

quote.description: Verbatim text that states the commencement date, at least 12 characters.

page.description: 1-based page of this document the quote is on (it may differ from the rent table's page).

confirmation.description: A person's confirmation of the parts of the value no quote can prove (a true/false value, an enum such as a CAM cap method or kick-out party, a paraphrased summary). With it, a candidate whose only gaps are such parts is verified with method human_verified: the parts the quote confirmed are listed under checked and the rest under confirmed_by_person. It never overrides a quote that is not on the page, a number or date the quote does not state, or a confidence below 0.8.

by.description: The name or role of the PERSON who read the clause and confirmed the value, e.g. "J. Smith, lease administrator". FactLot does not authenticate it. Never set this for a value no person has read: an agent must not confirm its own extraction.

at.description: When the person confirmed it: YYYY-MM-DD, or an ISO 8601 timestamp with offset. A date is recorded on the fact as that day at 00:00 UTC.

note.description: What the person checked; returned with the result (the fact schema has no field for it).

candidates.description: Values you extracted, each with its quote and page.

facts.description: Facts doc_verify_facts already returned for this document. With pages, each is checked again; without pages (to stay under the request size limit), only its value against its quote is checked and the abstract marks it quote_on_page: false.

items.description: A FactLot fact, as doc_verify_facts returned it.

documents.description: The lease and its amendments. Each needs pages with candidates or facts, or facts alone.

as_of.description: Date the facts are stated as of (YYYY-MM-DD), usually today.

subject.description: FactLot URN the facts are about, e.g. your lease's fl:lease:… ID. Default: the document ID.

tools.name: doc_compare
tools.title: Compare asserted values with a lease
tools.description: Compare values another document asserts (an estoppel, rent roll or offering memo, mapped by you to predicates) with verified lease facts from doc_abstract_lease or doc_verify_facts. Each asserted value comes back match, mismatch (with the differing fields), not_in_lease, or ambiguous_in_lease (two current lease facts disagree), with the controlling lease citation (document, page, quote). Values compare exactly as JSON: numbers by value, strings exactly (a name written differently is a mismatch), and for an object only the fields you assert. Facts another fact supersedes are ignored. When the lease fact is an extracted fact whose quote does not confirm part of its value (a true/false value, an enum), the result lists those parts in lease_not_checked. The lease facts must pass fact_validate; FactLot does not re-read the lease, so pass the facts its document tools returned.

items.description: A FactLot fact, as doc_verify_facts returned it.

lease_facts.description: Verified lease facts: the facts from doc_abstract_lease (or doc_verify_facts). Facts another fact supersedes are ignored.

predicate.description: Predicate of the asserted value, e.g. lease.expiration_date.

value.description: The asserted value in the predicate's shape (YYYY-MM-DD dates, plain numbers, decimal rates). For an object, only the fields given are compared.

asserted.description: Values another document states (an estoppel, a rent roll, an OM), mapped to predicates.

tools.name: doc_verify_claim
tools.title: Verify a claim against a document
tools.description: Check one claim against a document page: {predicate, value} (anything doc_verify_facts accepts) or a short claim sentence ({text} or a bare string), plus the verbatim quote and page it rests on. Returns supported (the quote is on the page and every checked number, date and name in the claim is written in it), contradicted (the quote is on the page and states other numbers or dates of the same kind, listed in quote_states), or unverifiable (the quote is not on the page, nothing in the claim can be checked, or the quote states no value of that kind), with the evidence (document_id, page, quote, span) and each part checked. Textual, not semantic: for a sentence only its numbers and dates are compared, never its meaning, and a quote that mentions the right number for a different term still supports it.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

document.description: The document the quote is from.

anyOf.description: A short claim sentence, read as {text: the sentence}; its numbers and dates are checked.

predicate.description: Predicate of the claim, with value.

value.description: Claimed value in the predicate's shape, with predicate.

text.description: Or a short claim sentence instead of predicate and value; its numbers and dates are checked.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page that the claim rests on.

tools.name: doc_spread_statement
tools.title: Spread an operating statement
tools.description: Spread a T-12, operating statement, budget or rent roll summary YOU read, onto FactLot's published chart of accounts (multifamily, commercial, or hotel after the USALI summary), deterministically; FactLot runs no model. Send the pages as text and one line per item: {label, amount, quote, page}, optionally your category, a period column, and for a subtotal the indexes of the lines it sums; give the statement's own totals (effective_gross_income, total_operating_expenses, net_operating_income, ebitda, ...) as lines with that total as category. Each line is checked: the quote is on the page (a quote under 12 characters, such as a short row, only where it stands as whole words), the amount (as a number, any common written form; (1,200) and -1,200 read as negative) and the label are written in it; a line that fails is excluded with the reason, and a stated total that does not foot names the lines left out. The label is mapped to the chart by keywords: your category is used when it is in the chart, and an exception flags it for review when the dictionary maps the label elsewhere; an ambiguous or unknown label without a category is excluded. Vacancy, concessions, credit loss and other contra lines are always subtracted. Returns per period the sections, the computed totals (EGI, operating expenses, NOI, capital items, net cash flow; for hotels departmental profit, GOP, EBITDA and NOI after the replacement reserve), whether each total and subtotal the statement states foots (within 0.5 per line added, or your tolerance), every line with its citation (document, page, quote, span) and status, statistics (units, occupancy, ADR), and exceptions to review. Not checked: whether the agent missed lines, and meaning beyond the written amount and label.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

property_type.description: Which chart of accounts to use: multifamily, commercial (office, retail, industrial), or hotel (USALI summary).

statement_type.description: What the document is; echoed back.

period.description: Default period label for lines that give none.

label.description: The line's label exactly as the statement writes it, e.g. "Real Estate Taxes". It must appear in the quote.

amount.description: The amount as a plain number (245000, not "$245K"). Write a deduction as the statement shows it; vacancy, concessions and other contra lines are always subtracted.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page with the label and the amount, e.g. "Real Estate Taxes 245,000". A row shorter than 12 characters ("R&M 310,411") is accepted where it appears on the page as whole words.

category.description: Your proposed category from the chart for property_type (spec/schemas/vocabularies/chart-of-accounts.json), e.g. real_estate_taxes, or a total such as net_operating_income for a total line. Without it, FactLot maps the label itself.

period.description: Period column the amount is from, e.g. "T-12 Sep 2026" or "2025". Lines are spread per period. Default: the statement's period.

sums.description: For a subtotal the statement prints ("Total Utilities"): the indexes (0-based) of the lines it adds up. FactLot checks that it foots.

lines.description: The statement's lines as you read them: every income, expense and capital line, the statement's own subtotals (with sums) and totals (with a total category), and statistics such as units or occupancy.

tolerance.description: Largest difference, in the statement's units, at which a subtotal or total still foots. Default: 0.5 for each line added (rounding).

tools.name: doc_check_use_conflict
tools.title: Check a proposed use against exclusives
tools.description: Check a proposed use (a description, plus an optional use category or 2022 NAICS code) against a center's verified lease.exclusive_use and lease.prohibited_uses facts (from doc_verify_facts or doc_abstract_lease; each must pass fact_validate). Deterministic and textual: a restriction is a potential conflict when it shares a use category with the proposed use (FactLot's published use-category vocabulary, matched on keywords, the category given and NAICS codes) or shares words with it (two or more, or every significant word of the restriction). Each hit is labelled "potential conflict — needs human review" and returns the controlling quote and citation, the categories and words that matched, and the exclusive's carve-outs, flagging those that mention the proposed use. FactLot does not interpret the lease, decide whether a carve-out applies, or give legal conclusions; an empty result does not mean there is no conflict. Superseded facts are ignored.

items.description: A FactLot fact, as doc_verify_facts or doc_abstract_lease returned it.

facts.description: Verified lease.exclusive_use and lease.prohibited_uses facts for the center, from doc_verify_facts or doc_abstract_lease (each must pass fact_validate). Facts another fact supersedes are ignored; other predicates are skipped.

text.description: The proposed use as described, e.g. "coffee shop selling espresso drinks and pastries".

category.description: Optional use category id from FactLot's vocabulary (spec/schemas/vocabularies/use-categories.json), e.g. coffee.

naics.description: Optional 2022 NAICS code, 2 to 6 digits; a shorter code matches every category under it (7225 matches restaurants and coffee shops).

tools.name: doc_predicates
tools.title: Lease predicate catalog
tools.description: Look up the lease predicates doc_verify_facts and doc_abstract_lease know (lease.expiration_date, lease.base_rent_schedule, lease.go_dark, ...) before extracting: for each, its value shape as JSON Schema, one valid example with a quote that states it (and whether that example verifies), which parts of the value are checked against the quote and how (number, ratio, date, verbatim name, as-written words, a worded enum, a number inside free text), which count as checked only when the quote writes them out (summaries, some enums), and which always need review (true/false values and enums no wording confirms, such as a CAM cap method or a kick-out party) unless a person confirms them. Generated from the same tables the checks use. Give predicate for one, prefix (e.g. lease.renewal) for a group, or neither for all. Also returns notes on statuses, paths, human confirmation and the generic rules for any other dotted predicate. Reads no document.

predicate.description: One predicate to describe, e.g. lease.go_dark. Omit both predicate and prefix for every lease predicate.

prefix.description: Only predicates starting with this, e.g. "lease.renewal" or "lease.". Give predicate or prefix, not both.

tools.name: fact_package_create
tools.title: Create a fact package
tools.description: Bundle FactLot facts (each must pass fact_validate) into a fact package a counterparty can verify: canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of every fact, an RFC 6962 Merkle tree over the facts, the source documents the facts cite with their sha256 where known, and a digest over all of it. Returns the unsigned package, its digest, and signing_message, the exact text to sign. FactLot never holds private keys: to sign, the holder signs signing_message with their own Ed25519 key on their own machine (factlot.sign_fact_package in Python, signFactPackage in @factlot/tools, or fact_package_sign in the local MCP server). Deterministic: no clock time is added (pass created_at), and the same facts always give the same digest.

items.description: A FactLot fact (it must pass fact_validate).

facts.description: The facts to package, in order: verified facts from the doc_* tools or any facts that pass fact_validate.

created_at.description: When the package was made (ISO 8601 with offset). FactLot adds no clock time, so the same input always gives the same package.

documents.description: Source documents to describe beyond what the facts cite (a title, the file's sha256). Every document a fact cites is listed automatically.

document_id.description: The document's ID as the facts cite it.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact file, when known.

tools.name: fact_package_verify
tools.title: Verify a fact package
tools.description: Verify a fact package from fact_package_create: recompute every fact's hash, the Merkle root and the digest from the content (any changed fact, title, date or document list shows as a mismatch); check each fact against fact_validate; check the Ed25519 signature, against the public_key you pass (base64url, the signer's key you trust) or, without one, only against the key inside the package (which proves nothing about who signed); and, given the source documents' pages, check every quote is on its cited page. Returns valid plus each check's details, checks_run and checks_not_run (what was and was not checked), and values_not_checked: the parts of extracted facts' values that their quotes do not confirm (a true/false value, an enum, a summary), which do not change valid. Not checked: that the pages you pass are the original files (pass sha256 to tie them to the file hash), or what the facts mean.

package.description: A fact package from fact_package_create, signed or not.

public_key.description: The signer's Ed25519 public key you trust: 32 bytes as base64url (a JWK's x). With it the signature must verify for the package to be valid.

documents.description: Optional: the source documents' pages (with sha256 when the facts cite the file's hash). Each fact's quote is then checked on its cited page.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

tools.name: lease_comp_validate
tools.title: Validate a lease comp and derive its NER
tools.description: Check a lease comparable one firm shares with others, as a FactLot fact with predicate lease.comp, and derive its net effective rent. The fact goes through fact_validate (schema, citations, rights), then the comp's own rules: shape (spec/schemas/fact.json LeaseComp: area, commencement, term or expiration, starting or current rent, escalation, free rent, TI, leasing commissions, expense basis, confirming party, verification), an expiration after commencement, a term that matches the dates, free rent within the term, no email, phone or ID number in the text. A comp names no person or company. With the default share profile it also needs the deal's starting rent, escalations, free rent, TI, property type, an expense basis other than unknown, and stated rights. When valid and a starting rent is given, ner.fact is a computed lease.net_effective_rent fact (formula calc.net_effective_rent@1, straight-line and discounted at discount_rate_annual, on the comp's own expense basis; no conversion between full service and net). Returns { valid, issues, warnings, ner }. Call before sharing a comp.

fact.description: A FactLot fact with predicate lease.comp: subject (an fl:lease: URN), value (the comp), as_of, provenance (with at least one source: your own record is fine, cited by document_id or sha256 without sharing it), and rights (ai_use and redistribution).

profile.description: share (default): a comp offered to other firms: needs the deal's starting rent, escalations, free rent, TI, expense basis, property type, a term and stated rights. observed: a rent seen in a public record (current_rent_psf_yr is enough); no NER is derived without a starting rent.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate for the discounted NER (an assumption, not part of the comp). 0 gives the straight-line NER only.

tools.name: lease_comp_search
tools.title: Search GSA lease comps (federal tenant)
tools.description: Search the 6,994 lease comps from the U.S. General Services Administration's Lease Inventory (October 2026 file, FactLot release lease-comps-gsa-2026-11-04), bundled with FactLot: works offline and on the hosted API, no registry needed. READ THE CAVEAT: the tenant in every one of these leases is the federal government (GSA, for an agency); they are not market comps for private tenants, and the rent is the current annual rent in GSA's file divided by the rentable SF, not the starting rent (no escalations, free rent, TI or commissions are known). Filter by state, 5-digit county FIPS, city, ZIP, a radius around a latitude/longitude (GSA's own coordinates; nothing is geocoded), rentable SF, commencement date, rent per SF, property type (office, industrial, other) and expense basis; sort; limit (default 25, at most 200). Each comp gives its FactLot lease ID, GSA lease number, address, county FIPS, building ID, landlord (organisations only; individuals are never stored), rentable SF, commencement, expiration, term, early-termination date, annual rent, rent per SF per year, property type, expense basis and the row of the GSA file it comes from. summary gives the count and the median, quartiles and range of rent per SF over every match, labelled as statistics of GSA leases. Every answer carries the caveat and the citation (GSA file URL, SHA-256 document ID, as-of and retrieval dates, licence: public domain). These are statistics of GSA leases, kept apart from market comps.

state.description: Two-letter state or territory code, e.g. "TX".

county_fips.description: 5-digit county FIPS code (state + county), e.g. "48201" for Harris County, Texas. Connecticut uses its planning regions (09110 to 09190).

city.description: City as GSA writes it, matched whole and ignoring case, e.g. "Houston".

near.description: Comps within a radius of a point, by great-circle distance to the coordinates GSA's file gives for each lease (FactLot geocodes nothing; give the point's coordinates yourself). Comps without coordinates are left out and counted in warnings.

min_rent_psf_yr.description: Lowest current rent, USD per rentable SF per year (GSA's current annual rent divided by the RSF).

max_rent_psf_yr.description: Highest current rent, USD per rentable SF per year.

property_type.description: office, industrial (GSA warehouse) or other (GSA special space): the largest use in the lease.

sort.description: Order of results: distance_asc (the default with near; needs near), commencement_desc (the default otherwise), commencement_asc, expiration_asc, expiration_desc, rent_psf_desc, rent_psf_asc, rentable_sf_desc, rentable_sf_asc. Ties go by GSA lease number.

limit.description: Maximum comps returned (1–200, default 25); the summary covers every match.

tools.name: registry_get
tools.title: Get a registry record
tools.description: Everything the FactLot Registry knows about a parcel, legal entity, or building: status, current cited facts (owner of record, situs address, property category, areas, values), ownership links, external IDs, and for a parcel the building it belongs to (condominium units roll up into one building). value_history (parcels) lists market and appraised value by tax year from every snapshot, newest first, each value cited; a tax year two snapshots value differently appears once per value. as_of gives the facts as they stood on a date. warnings flags area facts that look wrong (building area above 40 times the land area, a land area of 0); the facts themselves are as the source publishes them. A building record can carry debt.cmbs_loan facts (one per CMBS trust holding a note of its loan: balance, rate, maturity, payment status, servicer, special-servicing dates, NOI, DSCR) and an entity record can carry entity.parent facts (the SEC registrant that lists it as a subsidiary in Exhibit 21), each cited to its SEC filing. A miss says whether the county or entity registry is loaded. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the current roll year only in value_history and history (the answer says so); a Pro or Team key gets every year. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

urn.description: FactLot URN of a parcel, entity, or building, e.g. fl:parcel:us-48201:0011440000001 (Harris County, Texas) or fl:parcel:us-36061:1000020002 (Manhattan: a New York City borough-block-lot).

include_history.description: Also return every fact from every snapshot, superseded ones included (history lists current facts too; a source loaded once has no superseded facts).

as_of.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD): return the facts and ownership links current on that date, from the snapshots dated on or before it, instead of the latest. With include_history, history stops at that date. On the hosted API a dated lookup needs a Pro or Team key.

tools.name: registry_resolve_parcel
tools.title: Resolve a parcel in the registry
tools.description: Find a parcel's FactLot URN from state FIPS, county FIPS, and APN, if the registry holds it. A miss returns urn null with coverage: whether that county is loaded in this registry. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS, e.g. "48" for Texas, "36" for New York.

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS, e.g. "201" for Harris County, Texas, or "061" for New York County (Manhattan).

apn.description: Parcel or account number as the county prints it: an appraisal district account number in Texas, a borough-block-lot (e.g. 1000020002) in New York City, an AIN in Los Angeles County, a parcel number in San Francisco, a PID in Boston, a schedule number in Denver, the CAMA link in Connecticut.

tools.name: registry_resolve_external
tools.title: Resolve an external ID
tools.description: Find the FactLot URN for an ID from another system, e.g. system "sdat_account" (a Maryland SDAT account number), "hcad_account" (a Harris CAD account number), "nyc_bbl" (a New York City borough-block-lot), "la_ain" (a Los Angeles County Assessor ID number), "sf_parcel", "boston_pid", "denver_schednum" or "ct_cama_link". registry_coverage lists the systems a registry holds. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

system.description: Crosswalk system name, e.g. "sdat_account" (Maryland), "hcad_account" (Harris County, Texas) or "nyc_bbl" (New York City).

tools.name: registry_search_address
tools.title: Search parcels by address
tools.description: Find commercial parcels by situs address. Matches whole words of the street line (the part before the first comma), normalized: 'Street' = 'St', 'Northwest' = 'N.W.' = 'NW'; a suite, unit, '#' or floor is ignored. Give a house number ('1200 Main', '1200 Main St NW') or a street name with its type ('Main St'); a city or a part of a word alone matches nothing. After the first comma, give the city, state and ZIP code ('1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002'): a state (two letters or the full name) after a city or before a ZIP code, or a ZIP code ending the query, keeps the answer to that state (the ZIP code's when they disagree), those with the ZIP code first, then those in the city, then the rest of the state, before the limit is applied; a bare state with no city or ZIP code, and suite, floor or box text, are ignored. No match returns coverage: what this registry holds, in the named state when there is one. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

query.description: Street address ('1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002'), or a house number and street words, or a street name with its type; the city, state and ZIP code after the first comma narrow and order the matches.

tools.name: registry_search_entities
tools.title: Search legal entities by name
tools.description: Find registered business entities (LLCs, LPs, corporations) by name. Natural persons are not searchable. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

query.description: Entity name or part of one.

tools.name: registry_owned_by
tools.title: Parcels owned by an entity
tools.description: Commercial parcels currently linked to a legal entity as owner of record (inferred links carry a confidence), each with the building it belongs to, plus a per-building summary so condominium units count once per building. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

tools.name: registry_coverage
tools.title: What the registry holds
tools.description: The counties (with parcel and building counts), entity registries, and crosswalk systems this FactLot Registry file holds, each with its sources and as-of dates. Call it before concluding that a parcel or entity does not exist: a miss outside these regions means not loaded, not absent. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

tools.name: registry_tx_equity_candidates
tools.title: Texas unequal-appraisal candidates
tools.description: Candidate comparable parcels for a Texas unequal-appraisal comparison (Tax Code §41.43(b)(3)), from one tax year of the subject's appraisal district roll (the newest year whose roll gives the subject a value, or tax_year), with every field of the subject and the candidates read from that year's roll only: same county and tax year, the same state property category code, improvement area within area_band of the subject's, year built within year_band years when both are known; parcels sharing the subject's neighborhood code first (when the roll gives one), then its ZIP code, then the rest of the county if fewer than min_matches. Each candidate and the subject carry their roll fields (id, value and value_basis, market and appraised value, areas, year built, codes, situs address, tax year, citation of the value fact); the subject adds its value history by tax year. calc_args gives the same subject and candidates with exactly calc_tx_unequal_appraisal's input fields (tax_year, subject, comparables; id = the FactLot URN, label = the situs address, nulls left out, no adjustments): the candidate list under the default rule, not a selection by FactLot, for the caller to review and edit (remove, add or adjust comparables, each adjustment with a reason) before passing it to calc_tx_unequal_appraisal. Order of operations: registry_tx_equity_candidates, then the person's review, then calc_tx_unequal_appraisal with the reviewed calc_args, then report_create. selection echoes the rule, the effective parameters, the tax year and roll sources used, and which tier each candidate came from; selection_rule restates the parameters used (tax year, category, area band and year band with their bounds, counts per tier) with a notice that the list is the default rule's output. Each candidate's citation.document_id names its entry in sources, which gives that snapshot's license, attribution, ai_use and redistribution: relay them with the candidate. Candidates under FactLot's default rule, a design choice, not a legal standard; a person decides which, if any, to use. For evidence calculations only: FactLot does not represent property owners, file protests, or advise whether to protest. Not an appraisal or an opinion of value (Tex. Occ. Code §1103.003(1)); not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Never returns owner names, mailing addresses, or ownership facts: ownership is outside this comparison and is not needed for it. Texas parcels only. Tarrant County is not served by the hosted registry while the publisher's terms for AI use are unclear. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the current roll year only in the subject's value_history (the answer says so); the candidates are unchanged. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

urn.description: FactLot parcel URN of the subject, e.g. fl:parcel:us-48201:0011440000001. Give this, or county_fips and apn.

state_fips.description: With county_fips and apn: "48" (Texas), the only state served.

county_fips.description: 3-digit Texas county FIPS, e.g. "201" for Harris County.

apn.description: Appraisal district account number as the district prints it.

area_band.description: Improvement area band as a share of the subject's (0.35: within ±35%).

year_band.description: Year-built band in years, applied when both the subject's and the candidate's are known.

min_matches.description: Widen from the neighborhood and ZIP code tiers to the whole county when they hold fewer than this.

tax_year.description: Roll year to compare in. Default: the newest tax year whose roll gives the subject a positive value.

tools.name: registry_tx_equity_candidates_batch
tools.title: Texas unequal-appraisal candidates (batch)
tools.description: registry_tx_equity_candidates for many subjects in one call (1–50, e.g. a consultant's client parcels): each subject's id (your label, echoed back) and its urn, or county_fips and apn, plus the rule parameters once for every subject (area_band, year_band, min_matches, limit, tax_year). Each entry of results is that subject's answer from registry_tx_equity_candidates (subject, candidates, calc_args, selection, selection_rule, sources, warnings) or that subject's error (error, message, issues, and coverage on a miss), so one subject outside Texas, in Tarrant County, or not in the registry does not fail the others; the Texas-only and Tarrant checks apply to each subject. The selection rule and the notice appear once at the top (rule, notice) instead of in every answer; summary counts subjects, answered and errors. Candidates per subject only: this tool never runs calc_tx_unequal_appraisal and never picks comparables; a person decides, for each subject, which candidates (if any) to use, and only those go to calc_tx_unequal_appraisal (each subject's calc_args is its candidate list in that tool's input shape, for review and editing first). Relay each candidate's source rights from that subject's sources. For evidence calculations only: FactLot does not represent property owners, file protests, or advise whether to protest. Not an appraisal or an opinion of value (Tex. Occ. Code §1103.003(1)); not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Never returns owner names, mailing addresses, or ownership facts: ownership is outside this comparison. On the hosted API each answered subject counts as one registry lookup (a subject with an error is not counted), and this batch tool needs a Pro or Team key; registry_tx_equity_candidates, one subject per call, stays within the free daily lookups. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).
